title: Build and test a small life-administration inbox

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: An administration inbox separates action, deadline, dependency and confirmation. Filing a notice is not fulfilling it, and an unclear form should be routed for explanation before submission.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Complete fictional notices, today June 3: A—library renewal due June 8 at 17:00 through the existing account; confirmation screen appears after successful renewal. B—appointment June 6 at 10:00, confirm by June 4 at 12:00 through the clinic’s established message route. C—optional club newsletter with no reply required. No account credentials or clinical detail is supplied. Confirmation takes two minutes; renewal five.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Sort all three, schedule the real deadlines and prepare the smallest due action. Name the one location for confirmations before reading the result.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A renewal is prepared but the submit step fails. What status belongs in the inbox?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: B needs confirmation first, A needs renewal later, C may be read/filed/deleted by preference. Later fiction: B’s request is sent June 3 and receipt arrives, but appointment confirmation is still pending; A has not been attempted. Partial: calendar dates without response deadlines. Incorrect: mark receipt as confirmed or invent renewal. A folder can organize the trail without completing the work.
criteria: Action and deadline match each notice

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Prepared, submission failed, obligation still open. Preserve the deadline and use the service’s appropriate help/retry route; do not file it as completed because the form is filled.
criteria: Action and deadline match each notice
